intended_object: Given a projective representation ρ of G on V with factor set α (G acting trivially on kˣ), this is its linearization: the ordinary linear representation of the central extension E_α of G by kˣ on V, sending (a, g) to a·ρ(g). It is inferred from the docstring and the surrounding module.
explanation:
The definition composes `hρ.linearization htriv`, a monoid homomorphism E_α →* (V ≃ₗ[k] V) given by x ↦ x.left • ρ x.right, with Mathlib's `LinearEquiv.automorphismGroup.toLinearMapMonoidHom`, which sends each automorphism to its underlying linear map. The result is a `Representation k α.Extension V` acting by (a, g) · v = a • ρ(g) v. The companion lemma `linearizationRepresentation_apply` confirms this by `rfl`.

This is exactly the standard linearization of a projective representation through the central extension twisted by its factor set. On this extension the central kˣ acts by its own scalars, as `linearizationRepresentation_inl` records. Multiplicativity holds because the extension's multiplication is twisted by the same cocycle α that measures how far ρ is from being multiplicative.

The generality is natural: k is any commutative semiring, G any group and V any k-module. The trivial-action hypothesis is needed, because the extension is central and the factor set of a projective representation takes values in the central scalars.

Mathlib has no projective representations or this linearization, so there is no counterpart.
